playbook.strategy: Full-quota cooperation in this commons game produces a perfectly stable equilibrium where all boats harvest 3 each round, stock returns to 27 after each regrowth, and all players tie at identical scores. This episode confirms that alignment is rewarded over defection. On the first move of any new episode, signal cooperation by taking your full quota of 3; if all rivals match this signal in the first round, the pattern will likely sustain through remaining rounds. Do not underharvest to test rivals—that only leaves points on the table. Do not overharvest or dump unless you observe a rival clearly defecting (taking less than 2 or attempting to exceed 3). If the stock ever drops below 27 mid-round, check whether rivals' total catch is less than 9; if so, investigate whether someone is deliberately constraining catch or if the game rules differ from stated. The final round offers no endgame advantage—harvest normally. Always calculate the equilibrium early: if stock cap and regrowth rate allow all boats to take full quota without depleting, commit to that pattern and expect rivals to follow. Dumping is almost never profitable (−1 point) unless you can prove it denies an opponent 2+ points, which is rare in a symmetric game. Ties are acceptable outcomes and preferable to costly defection races.
